Preliminary GPU pool sizing (pilot -> scale), assuming your attached QPS:
- Pilot (weeks 1–4): 4 x A100-40GB (or 2 x H100-80GB if latency bound) — target 10–20k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Scale (months 2–6): 12–16 x A100-40GB equivalent (or 6–8 x H100) with 20% capacity cushion for peak spikes and canary lanes.
- Notes: If you expect sustained long sequences (>2k tokens), plan additional memory footprint per session and prefer H100.

Lead time estimates (ballpark):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool on cloud): 6–8 weeks from signed commit to production routing (shorter if onboarding to existing region/reserved pool).
- Redwood Private (VPC + managed control plane): 10–14 weeks for cloud VPC setups; 14–20 weeks for on-prem rack delivery (procurement + rack + networking + KMS integration).

I'll attach the initial MAP and the draft technical notes — Marcus, can you confirm the network/NAT requirements and quantization guidance? Monica, I'll need the pricing band we discussed for a 6-month committed pilot so Samir has numbers to evaluate.

Best,

Elena / Hannah — technical notes from my side (summarized):

1) Private vs Dedicated considerations:
- Dedicated (hosted) is fastest: we can wire into an existing Redwood region and provision reserved instances; we recommend a canary pool (10% of requested capacity) for rollout testing.
- Private (VPC): network peering, KMS key policies, and TLS mutual auth need planning. For on-prem racks, plan 2–3 weeks extra for rack staging + security hardening.

2) Sizing & performance knobs:
- For transformer models with batch-optimized runtime, expect 1.6–2.2x throughput on H100 vs A100 for identical model weights. If you can tolerate slightly higher latency, A100 saves cost.
- Suggest starting pilot with mixed-instance footprint (2 x H100 + 2 x A100) to validate latency-sensitive paths and cost curves.
- KV cache warmup: include a 48–72 hour warmup window during pilot to collect realistic cache hit patterns.

3) Networking/storage:
- Persistent KV caches require an NFS or S3-like tier; prefer S3 for durability but prepare for a short warmup penalty.
- Firewall: outbound to redwood-control-plane.redwood-inference.com:443 and inbound from our telemetry edge only.

4) Operational runbook items (canary -> full route):
- Week 0: infra provisioning + baseline perf tests.
- Week 1–2: smoke test & latency SLAs.
- Week 3–4: stability testing, quality evals against your prompt set.

Attaching a short notes PDF.

Marcus

Samir — thanks for the procurement checklist. Below are concrete answers and next steps (we've updated the MAP to v2 and dropped it in the Drive link):

1) Partial reservation + expansion: yes — we support an initial reserved commit with an elastic expansion clause. Typical minimum for a committed pilot is 4 reserved GPU equivalents; we can stamp the contract to allow stepped increases with 30 days notice for capacity reallocation.

2) Pricing: Monica, see action item to attach 6-month pilot quote (committed vs burst). Monica: will provide two bands (pilot committed pricing, on-demand overage) and a committed discount schedule tied to DL-2026-4589.

3) SLA / compliance: Dedicated comes with an uptime SLA and token-latency targets (commercial annex). Private customers get the same controls but SLAs are applied to the control plane we manage; for on-prem the SLA scope is narrower. SOC2 and audit artifacts can be provided after an NDA — we'll share a redacted SOC2 pack during evaluation.

MAP milestones & owners (high level):
- Week A (Provisioning): Redwood provision reserved pilot capacity + Helix network/KMS prep — owners: Redwood (Hannah/Marcus), Helix (Elena/Samir).
- Week B (Pilot start): Baseline perf + smoke tests — owners: Marcus / Helix infra.
- Week C (Quality gating): Evaluate prompt-set regressions (Helix data team) — owners: Helix, Redwood to provide eval harness.
- Decision window (End of week 6): Proceed to scale OR revise sizing/pricing.
